Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Aether Brands Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Aether Brands Inc.'s Q3 2024 results. With me on the call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Innovation Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. Aether Brands delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Today, we'll walk through our overall company performance highlights, performance across key categories and brands, new product launches and innovation pipeline, price elasticity insights, supply chain efficiencies and productivity savings, promotional strategy and effectiveness, and gross margin guidance with key assumptions. I'll now turn the call over to Mike Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Mike Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. As Sarah mentioned, we delivered a standout quarter amid a challenging macroeconomic backdrop. Net sales reached $14.5 billion, up 6.7% year-over-year and 6.3% organically excluding FX and minor acquisitions. This topped our guidance, powered by 2.8% volume growth, 3.2% pricing, and 0.3% favorable mix. Adjusted diluted EPS hit $1.62, up 10% and ahead of expectations, thanks to tight cost controls and productivity gains.

Gross margins expanded 180 basis points to 48.2%, the best in three years, driven by supply chain optimizations like 15% lower ocean freight via rerouted Asia-Pacific networks and $285 million in year-to-date productivity savings from our Project Velocity AI forecasting tool, now covering 85% of factories. This countered 4% commodity inflation in areas like cocoa and palm oil, where we've hedged 70% of FY24 needs. Adjusted operating income climbed 12% to $2.85 billion, with margins at 19.7%, up 100 basis points. SG&A deleveraged to 16.3% of sales through zero-based budgeting and digital trade tools boosting retailer velocity 8% at Walmart and Kroger. EBITDA margins reached 24.2%, on track for mid-20s long-term.

Let me dive deeper into performance by key categories and brands, which shows the strength of our portfolio. We divide into four pillars: Beauty & Personal Care, Food & Snacks, Beverages, and Home Care, totaling $14.5 billion, up 7.2% reported and 6.8% organic—beating the CPG average of 3.5% per IRI and Nielsen. Beauty & Personal Care, 32% of sales at $4.6 billion, grew 9.1% organically on premiumization, with high-end up 15% versus flat mass. LuminaGlow skincare, our anti-aging hero with hyaluronic acid and peptides, boosted U.S. household penetration to 28% from 24% via the "Glow from Within" campaign and 2,500 new Ulta and Sephora doors. Margins rose 120 basis points to 22.5% from AI inventory tools cutting North America stockouts 35%. APAC surged 14% with 25% e-comm in China on Tmall and JD.com; EMEA held 41% ACV despite 2% inflation headwinds using value packs.

Food & Snacks, 28% at $4.0 billion, up 6.5% organically, led by 5.2% volumes in at-home snacking. NutriCrunch plant-based bars with 15g protein grew 22% to $450 million, grabbing 12% better-for-you share per SPINS, thanks to keto flavors and 40% recycled packaging. Pricing up 2.8% offset 5% YoY cocoa and nut inflation. North America gained 1.2 share points to 37% in savory snacks with 1.5x ROI promotions; LATAM at 3% countered Brazil FX via 10% local sourcing cuts.

Beverages hit $3.2 billion, up 8.4% organically, fastest grower on functional trends. HydraBoost electrolyte water with vitamins and no sugar jumped 28% to $650 million in the $12 billion U.S. market growing 11% CAGR per Beverage Digest. Non-caloric sweeteners lifted trial 18%; pricing 3.1%, volumes 4.2% via 15,000 Walmart/Kroger coolers. North America 11%, DTC 8%; EMEA -1% offset by "Beat the Heat" and Aldi ties.

Home Care at $2.7 billion, up 4.2%, strong in disinfectants. PureShield cleaner grew 12% to $380 million, +2.1 share to 29% per Nielsen, with Amazon Subscribe & Save at 22% volume. Margins steady at 24% despite 7% surfactant inflation via Singapore hub hedging 80% FY24 for $150 million savings. APAC 9% on India urbanization with hard-water formulas; Europe 2% pivoting to enzyme alternatives.

These results highlight our "Power Brands, Premium Growth" approach: top 20 brands drove 80% organic growth via $450 million marketing and 12 launches, three in health & wellness. Sustainability advances to 100% recyclable packaging by 2027, with LuminaGlow at 65%. Omnichannel at 28% up from 22%, AI personalization lifting repeats 14%. We see 5-7% Q4 organic growth with easing inflation.

Shifting to price elasticity observations, a key part of our strategy. Across our portfolio, elasticity averaged -0.45, meaning 1% ASP rise led to 0.45% volume drop—more inelastic than pre-pandemic -0.65, aiding 4.2% revenue growth despite 2.1% volume softness. Household essentials like laundry were ultra-inelastic at -0.25; 6% ASP hike eroded volumes just 1.5%, slowing private label to 1.2%. Snacks at -0.75 saw 3% ASP cause 2.3% drop, mitigated by 2% rollbacks recapturing 150 bps share. Beverages -0.55, with 5% up on functionals losing only 2.7% volumes. North America -0.40 improved 15% QoQ; Europe -0.55; emerging -0.30.

Our AI elasticity models on IRI/Nielsen data cut forecast errors 25%; tiered pricing protects core SKUs, trade depth down 18% for 22% ROI lift. Q4 elasticity to -0.50 with 2-3% ASP moderation.

On promotional strategy and effectiveness, trade spend at 22.4% of sales, down 150 bps, yielded 3.8x ROI and 14% lift versus 10-12% industry. 60% to event-driven TPRs/displays; 1,200 events in beverages captured 28% ACV, 4.2x ROI in North America via PromoOptix AI. North America 4.1x on EDLP-plus; EMEA 3.5x digital loyalty; APAC/LatAm 3.9-4.5x hyper-local. Shopper Insights Engine cut fatigue 20%; promos drove 42% of 5.2% growth, margins +110 bps. FY24 at 21-23%, targeting 4x+ ROI.

Finally, gross margin guidance for FY24: 150-200 bps expansion to 48.5-49.5%, strongest in five years post FY23's 47.0%. Assumptions: inputs +1.5-2.0%, cocoa hedged 70% at $4,200/MT despite $6,000 spot; sugar flat, palm down 5-7%. Pricing 4.0-4.5% net, elasticity -0.4x better than -0.6x category. Volume/mix +2-3% organic with 1.5% premium tailwind; power brands 65% revenue at higher margins. Supply chain $250M savings (125 bps): AI procurement, plant closures to 88% OEE, freight down 15-20%, nearshoring. North America 48.5-49.5%; Europe 46-47%; emerging 44-45%. Risks: cocoa to $7,000 (+25 bps); upside sugar deflation. Positions for 50%+ by FY26.

We've raised FY24 guidance: organic sales 5.5-6.0%, EPS $6.45-6.55, FCF $4.2B, 100+ bps share gains.

Following my remarks, Lisa will update on marketing and brand performance.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Mike. We continue to see strong performance across key brands. Our marketing investments drove higher consumer engagement, especially the "Glow from Within" campaign lifting LuminaGlow penetration. Premiumization and health trends propelled snacks like NutriCrunch and beverages like HydraBoost, with targeted promotions yielding high ROI and velocity gains in club and e-comm channels. We're optimizing omnichannel personalization for repeat loyalty.

After me, Raj will discuss supply chain initiatives.

Raj Singh:
Thank you, Lisa. Our focus on supply chain optimization delivered $285 million YTD savings, 12% better than last year, adding 85 bps to margins against 7% palm/PET inflation. COGS down 6.5% via yields and scrap cuts; logistics $120M from 15% freight reductions, 98.5% OTIF. Productivity up 11%, inventory turns 9.8x freeing $450M cash.

Digital twin on SAP/Blue Yonder cut forecast error 28%, safety stock 18%; AMRs boosted picks 35%; procurement with Cargill/Wilmar at 5-7% below market, 15% Mexico nearshoring. Sustainability like regenerative ag cut water 14%. North America 15% logistics wins; EMEA offset energy hikes; APAC 18% uplift. FY24 100-150 bps expansion via GenAI maintenance.

Finally, Dr. Vasquez will share on innovation.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Raj. We're excited about new product launches and our pipeline. Q3's 12 SKUs added $145M, 8.2% of sales; YTD $420M, 22% growth. Aether Veggie Crunch hit 15% HUT, 2.1 share in savory snacks at 78% ACV, 42% margins. Pulse Ignite energy $68M, 45% QoQ, 25% Gen Z trial. EcoGlow skincare €32M, 12% natural care share.

Pipeline: 28 SKUs, $750M potential, via Cincinnati center's AI cutting timelines to 9 months, precision fermentation for alt-dairy Q1 2025. 70% regenerative sourcing. North America 55%; EMEA PFAS-free; APAC affordable premium; LATAM indulgence. Innovation 12% sales to 15% FY26, 70/20/10 rule.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. The floor is now open for questions. Our first question comes from John Smith with Bank of America.

John Smith:
Can you provide an update on your efforts to reduce packaging waste and the associated cost savings?

Raj Singh:
Thanks for the question, John. Packaging waste reduction is core to our sustainability and efficiency goals. Through light-weighting—like 10% less PET per bottle—and 100% recyclable targets by 2027, we've hit 65% compliance on LuminaGlow already. Reusable trials with Tesco saved $12M in materials; regenerative sourcing and post-consumer recycled use in NutriCrunch cut costs while qualifying for EU CBAM credits. YTD, this embedded $40M in savings within our $285M productivity, directly aiding 85 bps margin lift. Nearshoring and dynamic routing further slashed logistics waste, with plans for GenAI predictive maintenance to preempt downtime and extend asset life.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen:
How are you leveraging data analytics to personalize your marketing efforts and improve customer engagement?

Lisa Patel:
Great question, Emily. Data analytics is transforming our personalization. Our TradeAI and PromoOptix platforms use IRI/Nielsen, POS, and 500M loyalty transactions for hyper-local assortment, lifting promo ROI 18-22% and repeats 14%. App-based insights boosted EcoGlow loyalty 15%; WeChat Mini Programs in APAC cut cannibalization 15%, driving 18% lifts. Shopper Insights Engine caps promo fatigue, converting 22% promo buyers to repeats in EMEA. Omnichannel at 28% sales, with elasticity modeling enabling targeted TPRs yielding 4x ROI.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Citi.

David Kim:
What is the expected impact of recent commodity price increases on your gross margins?

Mike Chen:
David, commodity spikes like cocoa at $6,000+ spot are a watch item, but we've hedged 70% through mid-2024 at $4,200/MT, mitigating 60% run-up. Blended FY24 inflation at 1.5-2.0%, netting 50 bps drag—cocoa outlier up 25%, offset by sugar flat and palm down 5-7%. Supply chain $250M savings add 125 bps; pricing 4-4.5% 175 bps. Risks like $7,000/MT add 25 bps downside, but structural levers position for 48.5-49.5% guidance.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rossi with Barclays.

Mike Rossi:
Can you discuss the competitive landscape and any emerging trends that are impacting your market share?

Sarah Thompson:
Mike, thanks. We're gaining share—100+ bps targeted FY24—via premiumization, where power brands like LuminaGlow and HydraBoost grew 80% of organic sales, outpacing private labels. Health/wellness trends, functional beverages at 11% CAGR, plant-based snacks; sustainability with regenerative ag hedging volatility. Innovation 22% YTD growth; omnichannel 28%. Peers face similar inflation, but our elasticity -0.45, productivity outpacing by 200 bps, and localized strategies counter discounters. Emerging trends like clean beauty, alt-proteins position us strongly.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your thoughtful questions and participation. We are confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to updating you next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Aether Brands Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
